focus.jtag: October CPI printed yesterday (core +0.3%), stocks dipped 0.38% but stayed calm and the VIX eased to 19.46. Overnight, CoreWeave's beat lit a tech rebound — S&P futures +0.9%, Nasdaq +1.9%. Bonds are closed for Veterans Day. The scanner boarded 5 names
focus.jnote: The data overhang cleared, and overnight the tape turned risk-on — but a holiday thins the plumbing. The S&P 500 fell 0.38% to 7,520.93 and the Nasdaq dropped 0.74% to 25,065.88, while the Dow lost 0.3% to 52,231.89. The culprit was inflation: core prices rose 0.3% for a third straight month, and have now risen 0.3% or more in 5 of 2026's first 10 months. That hit the Fed's marker — as of late Tuesday CME FedWatch priced an 88.8% chance of 25bp in December and 11.2% of 50, with a hold at zero. Yet equities stayed composed and the VIX closed at 19.46 on Tuesday, down 2.31% from Monday's 19.92, remaining below the 20 level but above the calm conditions seen before last week's spike. Overnight the mood flipped bullish on earnings — Nasdaq-100 futures advanced 1.9%, while S&P 500 futures climbed 0.9% — after CoreWeave announced robust Q3 results, with revenue soaring 168% year-over-year to $3.7 billion, substantially beating guidance. One caveat for today: it is Veterans Day, so U.S. stocks are open but cash Treasuries are shut — thinner liquidity and wider spreads.
focus.notdown: The scanner boarded two bullish Type A post-earnings gaps and two Type C breakouts. The cleanest fundamentally is CRWV (Type A, Grade A) on a monster double-beat and raised guidance — but note the realized gap matched the full implied move, so the easy money may be made, and liquidity isn't verified. DHT (Type A, Grade A) is a record tanker quarter but gapped on light volume. The two breakouts, JAN and G (both Type C, Grade A), have held their pivots two sessions on heavy volume. On a half-size day, validate each at 9:35 ET before entry.
focus.notup: No bearish Snipers boarded today. No fresh post-earnings down-gap on a double-miss-plus-cut cleared the filters, and no durable negative named catalyst qualified. Selling bear calls into a tape where futures are ripping ~1–2% on a CoreWeave-led tech rebound invites a squeeze. The disciplined answer on the bearish side is to sell nothing new today.
focus.why: Why YELLOW (not GREEN)? The gap math supports risk-taking — P(≥1% gap) ~31% is below the 35% trigger and composite 44 is comfortably MILD. But two frictions keep it out of GREEN: it is Veterans Day, so cash Treasuries are shut while equities trade, thinning liquidity and widening option spreads, and the hot core print keeps a 50bp December hike live. With 5 names boarded, the right posture is half size, A-grade only, validate at 9:35 ET — take the best, skip the rest, and keep every spread's DTE clear of its next print.

setups.read: Fresh post-earnings gap up on a record tanker quarter. DHT reported Q3 profit after tax of $270.9 million, versus $44.8 million a year earlier and $198.3 million in Q2. Net income came in at $270.9 million, equal to $1.68 per share, and management guided Q4 to top Q3 for a new annual record. The concern: the gap came on very light relative volume (~0.01x), well below the 1.3x confirmation bar — and the stock's move was muted despite the beat. Catalyst is 2 sessions old. Only 1 S/R layer (gap floor ~$20.81). Treat as A-grade but validate hard.

setups.read: The cleanest fundamental catalyst on the board. CoreWeave reported Q3 revenue up 168% year-over-year to $3.7 billion, substantially beating guidance, and raised full-year revenue guidance to $13.0–$13.3 billion and lifted adjusted operating income guidance. The stock moved +7.9% on the report. Two cautions: the scanner flagged the realized gap matched the full ~15% implied move (easy money may be done), liquidity was NOT verified, and a scanner note referenced a guidance-cut tag that conflicts with the raise — confirm the chain and the guidance read on your platform before entry.

risks: Veterans Day thin liquidity — U.S. stocks are open but cash Treasuries are shut. Thinner volume and wider option spreads mean worse fills and bigger slippage on any new spread — the number-one practical risk today.

Hot-core CPI & a live 50bp hike — core prices rose 0.3% for a third straight month, which puts an 11.2% market-implied chance of a 50bp December move on the table alongside the 88.8% priced for 25bp. Rate-sensitive names (the JAN REIT especially) carry added gap risk.
Yields jumped on the print — the 10-year yield rose to 4.98% as the S&P fell 0.38%. With cash bonds closed today there's no live yield signal — a gap when they reopen Thursday is a hidden risk.

CRWV liquidity unverified & crowded — the scanner did not confirm CoreWeave's option chain, IV is ~106%, and the name appears twice on the board (Type A and Type B). Don't double up; verify the chain before entry.
CSCO & AMAT · Thu 11/12 AMC — Cisco and Applied Materials report Thursday after the close; AMAT is a direct read on the chip/AI capex cycle. Keep any tech/semis spread's DTE clear of these prints.
